### 2. Time Series Data
library(tidyverse)
## 2.2
## a.
#retail_raw <- read.csv("data/retail_sales_raw.csv")
#head(retail_raw)
## b.
retail_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/retail_sales_raw.csv",
  na = ".",
  col_types = cols(
    observation_date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    RSAFS = col_double(),
    RSAFSNA = col_double()
  )
)
head(retail_raw)

## 2.3
retail_raw_long <- retail_raw |>
  select(observation_date, RSAFS, RSAFSNA) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(RSAFS, RSAFSNA), names_to = "series_id", values_to = "sales")
head(retail_raw_long)

## 2.4
library(fpp3)

retail_ts <- retail_raw_long |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(observation_date)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month, key = series_id)
head(retail_ts)

## 2.5
### a.
head(canadian_gas)
key_vars(canadian_gas)
index_var(canadian_gas)
### b.
can_gas <- canadian_gas |>
  select(Month, Volume)

has_gaps(can_gas)
head(can_gas)

## 2.6
### a.
can_gas_recent <- can_gas |>
  filter(Month >= yearmonth("1990 Jan"))

head(can_gas_recent)
### b.
can_gas_recent <- can_gas_recent |>
  mutate(year    = year(Month),
         month   = month(Month, label = TRUE),
         quarter = quarter(Month))
head(can_gas_recent)

can_gas_recent |>
  as_tibble() |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarize(avg_volume = mean(Volume))
### c.
can_gas_recent |>
  mutate(next_month           = Month + 1,
         same_month_last_year = Month - 12) |>
  head()
### d.
can_gas_q <- can_gas |>
  filter(Month <= yearmonth("2004 Dec")) |>
  index_by(Quarter = yearquarter(Month)) |>
  summarize(Volume = sum(Volume))

head(can_gas_q)
can_gas_q |> autoplot(Volume)

## 2.7
### a.
retail_ts |> autoplot(sales)
### b.
retail_ts |>
  autoplot(sales) +
  labs(
    title = "U.S. Retail and Food Services Sales",
    subtitle = "Seasonally adjusted vs. not seasonally adjusted",
    x = NULL, y = "Millions of dollars", color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

The NSA series displays a prominent, sharp spike every December due to holiday shopping, followed by a drop in January. The SA series removes this predictable annual spike, smoothing out the intraday seasonal swings so that the underlying economic trend and recessionary drops are clearer.

### c.
can_gas |> 
  autoplot(Volume) +
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Natural Gas Production (1960–2005)",
    x = NULL, 
    y = "Volume (Billions of cubic meters)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
  
### d.
can_gas |> 
  autoplot(Volume) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Natural Gas Production with Trend Line",
    x = NULL, 
    y = "Volume (Billions of cubic meters)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
  
Added geom_smooth() to overlay a non-linear trend line across the entire historical period, making it easy to identify long-term structural increases in output over time.
